import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on products
df['Total_Mnt'] = df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + \
                  df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds']

# Drop rows with missing Income values, as Income is crucial for this visualization
df_filtered = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])

# Filter out potential outliers in Income and Total_Mnt for better visualization of the main distribution
# Remove incomes that are extremely low or high, and customers with zero spending
df_filtered = df_filtered[
    (df_filtered['Income'] > 1000) &
    (df_filtered['Income'] < 150000) &
    (df_filtered['Total_Mnt'] > 0)
]

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Mnt',
    hue='Marital_Status',
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    s=60,  # Size of the markers
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for better distinction of points
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title('Customer Spending vs. Income by Marital Status', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=12)

# Position the legend outside the plot area
plt.legend(title='Marital Status', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Ensure all elements fit tightly within the figure area
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
